sections.title: Learning techniques
sections.content:
Effective strategies for building advanced vocabulary:
• Context clues — Use surrounding words to guess meaning. Even if you don't know a word, context often reveals its meaning.
• Word families — Learn related forms together: succeed, success, successful, successfully. Knowing word families multiplies your vocabulary efficiently.
• Collocations — Learn words in natural pairs: make a decision, do research. Collocations make your English sound more natural and fluent.
• Spaced repetition — Review words at increasing intervals. Spaced repetition helps transfer vocabulary to long-term memory.
• Active use — Use new words in your own sentences. Writing sentences with new words strengthens retention dramatically.

sections.title: Common pitfalls
sections.content:
Mistakes to avoid when learning vocabulary:
• False friends — Words that look similar across languages but mean different things. Be careful with false friends between your language and English.
• Register errors — Using formal words in casual settings. Using 'commence' in casual conversation sounds unnatural.
• Overuse of basic words — Relying on 'good', 'bad', 'nice'. Replace basic adjectives with precise ones: 'outstanding', 'dreadful', 'delightful'.
• Ignoring connotation — Not understanding emotional overtones. 'Slim' is positive, 'skinny' can be negative, though both mean thin.

exercises.question: Using words around an unknown word to guess its meaning uses:
exercises.explanation: Context clues are hints found in surrounding text that help determine word meaning.

exercises.question: Words that look similar in two languages but have different meanings are:
exercises.explanation: False friends are words in different languages that look similar but have different meanings.

exercises.question: Words that naturally go together (like 'make a decision') are:
exercises.explanation: Collocations are words that are commonly used together in natural English.

exercises.question: Reviewing words at increasing time intervals is:
exercises.explanation: Spaced repetition is reviewing information at gradually increasing intervals.

exercises.question: The emotional feeling a word carries beyond its definition is its:
exercises.explanation: Connotation is the emotional or cultural association a word carries.

exercises.question: Using overly formal words in casual conversation is a ___ error:
exercises.explanation: A register error means using language at an inappropriate level of formality.

exercises.question: Learning succeed, success, successful together uses:
exercises.explanation: Word families are groups of words with a shared root (e.g., educate, education, educational).

exercises.question: Writing your own sentences with new words is called:
exercises.explanation: Active use means practising vocabulary by producing it in your own sentences.
